title: Aftermath of Death
next_chapter_hook: Just as the three parties were arguing endlessly, Ling Yuan suddenly said something that shocked everyone: 'He's not dead, you're all idiots'

text.content: Above the ruins of the Dragon Vein, smoke and dust had yet to settle. The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor brushed the焦灰 from his sleeve, wearing an air of absolute dominance, as if the earth-shattering explosion moments ago was merely entertainment after a meal. 'Everyone look—' He pointed to the charred corpse. 'The Demonic Path remnant Chen Ji has been slayed by this one on the spot!' The surrounding cultivators exchanged uncertain glances, some secretly stepping back, unwilling to get involved in this mess. The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor remained oblivious, continuing his grand speech as if the world had already been conquered and his name deserved top honors.

dialogue.content: Just then, an impatient voice came from the back of the crowd: 'What a large face the Crown Prince's Grand Tutor has.' Han Lie pushed through the crowd, his face full of mockery. 'I saw the Dragon Vein explode with my own eyes, and you ran faster than anyone. Now you claim you killed him?' He crossed his arms and sneered. 'If thistrash really was killed by you, why don't you dare go verify the body?'

text.content: The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor's expression stiffened, then he coldly snorted: 'Young Master Han, do not speak nonsense. This one bears the Emperor's command, eliminating Demonic Path remnants is my duty, why must I explain to anyone?' He shifted his tone, becoming sinister. 'But the Holy Sect will have to give an explanation to the world. The Dragon Vein's awakening, Chen Ji's rebellion—these two great calamities cannot be unrelated to them!' This speech immediately stirred an uproar, and the cultivators who had merely been watching now began discussing heatedly.

dialogue.content: At the edge of the crowd, a figure shrouded in black mist stood quietly. It was a Demonic Path secret agent, who watched the entire spectacle with a faint mocking curve at the corner of his lips. News of Chen Ji's death should have been good news to him, yet the ugly display before his eyes made it seem utterly ridiculous. He silently took out a communication Jade Slip and carved everything he witnessed—the absurd scene of three parties fighting for credit—into it word for word.

text.content: Meanwhile, behind a collapsed stone tablet in the depths of the ruins, Chen Ji sat cross-legged, surrounded by faint traces of Dragon Vein's remaining energy. His robes were charred and torn, his face black and white, looking like a beggar who had just crawled out of a stove. Yet his eyes were clear and bright, even carrying a theatrical amusement. 'Interesting.' He murmured to himself. 'Let them continue making a scene.'

choice.prompt: The dispute between the Crown Prince's Grand Tutor and Han Lie grows increasingly intense. What will you do?

choices.description: Let them continue fighting amongst themselves and see what kind of mess they can create.
choices.risk_hint: May miss the opportunity to intervene

text.content: Chen Ji's lips curved slightly as he redirected his attention to the spectacle. The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor was grabbing Han Lie's collar to interrogate him, but Han Lie made him retreat with just one look—the gap in Combat Power reduced the latter to making fierce but empty threats. 'Wonderful.' Chen Ji silently uttered these two words.

choices.text: Add fuel to the fire in secret
choices.description: Since they love credit so much, let them compete even more fiercely.

text.content: Chen Ji's fingertips moved slightly, and an almost invisible energy current quietly entered the ruins. The next moment, the rubble beneath the Crown Prince's Grand Tutor suddenly shifted, causing him to stumble and lunge toward Han Lie—'You dare push me?!' Han Lie roared in anger, both palms launching sharp energy. The two immediately engaged in combat, and the surrounding crowd cried out in alarm as they scattered in all directions.

dialogue.content: In the chaos, Chen Ji's spiritual sense caught an unusual fluctuation. Following that aura, he saw several figures quietly approaching the 'corpse'—they were the Empire's Shadow Guards. Their movements were swift and their coordination seamless, clearly part of a premeditated plan. Chen Ji blinked, sighing internally: 'Want to use my corpse as a bargaining chip? Bold idea.' He restrained his impulse to act and wanted to see what these people intended to do.

The battle between the Crown Prince's Grand Tutor and Han Lie was nearing its end. The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor was sent stumbling back several zhang by Han Lie's palm, falling to the ground in a sorry state, a trace of blood at the corner of his mouth. 'Han Lie! How dare you attack an imperial official!' He screamed furiously. Han Lie shook his wrist and laughed carelessly: 'You call yourself an imperial official? A person riding on tiger's prestige, dares to jump around in front of me?'

text.content: Just at this moment, an elderly yet commanding voice descended from the heavens: 'Enough.' Everyone looked up to see Ling Yuan walking through the air, his robes billowing, with the bearing of a grand master. He landed in the center of the ruins, his gaze sweeping over everyone present, finally fixing on the charred corpse with an indecipherable expression. 'The Dragon Vein is destroyed, Chen Ji is dead.' His voice was terrifyingly calm. 'Instead of handling aftermath, why are you all attacking each other? What a disgrace!'

choice.prompt: After Ling Yuan appears, what will you do?

choices.description: This old fox Ling Yuan arrived too conveniently, perhaps he sensed something long ago. Observe the situation first.

text.content: Chen Ji收敛气息，concealing himself deeper into the shadows. Ling Yuan's words appeared to be quelling the dispute, but every sentence was actually stabbing at the hearts of the Crown Prince's Grand Tutor and Han Lie. He narrowed his eyes, noticing that Ling Yuan's gaze kept glancing toward his 'corpse' direction. 'Old fox.' He sneered in his heart. 'Indeed, ill-intentioned.'

choices.description: The show was entertaining enough, but this old fox Ling Yuan is not easy to deal with. Know when to quit.

text.content: Chen Ji silently moved backward, preparing to leave this trouble spot. However, the instant he turned, a lingering sense of being watched made his hair stand on end. He sharply turned back, just in time to meet Ling Yuan's deep, unfathomable eyes—that gaze seemed capable of piercing through all illusion, directly reaching the corner where he hid.

Ling Yuan withdrew his gaze, his expression unreadable. He slowly walked toward the charred corpse, bent to examine it for a moment, his brow creasing tighter and tighter. 'Strange.' He murmured to himself, his voice low yet clearly heard by everyone present. 'On this corpse, there is not even a trace of Heavenly Fate residue...' At these words, the entire crowd erupted. The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor's face turned pale, and Han Lie also dropped his playful expression, his demeanor becoming grave.

dialogue.content: Han Lie stepped forward several paces, staring at the corpse for a long while, then suddenly burst into cold laughter: 'What does this mean, Sect Master Ling? Could you be saying this corpse isn't Chen Ji?' He turned to scan the crowd. 'Or perhaps—someone is being fraudulent, deceiving us all?' At these words, everyone's gaze focused on the Crown Prince's Grand Tutor. The old man's face was livid, his lips trembling, yet for a moment he didn't know how to defend himself.

text.content: On the other side of the ruins, the Empire's Shadow Guards had also stopped their movements. The leader exchanged a glance with his companion, then quietly retreated toward the edge of the crowd. Chen Ji's spiritual sense caught this scene, and he coldly thought: 'It seems even within the Empire, someone doesn't trust this 'great contributor'.' He quietly followed those figures, wanting to hear what message they would transmit.

choice.prompt: The Empire's Shadow Guards are about to transmit intelligence. What will you do?

choices.description: The Empire's intelligence network is not to be underestimated. Let's hear what they have to say.

text.content: Chen Ji收敛气息，quietly approaching those Shadow Guards. He heard the leaderwhispered道: 'Immediately report to the court—the Crown Prince's Grand Tutor's statements appear fraudulent. Since the corpse bears no Heavenly Fate residue, it proves Chen Ji likely did not die. The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor, in his haste for merit, may ruin major matters.' Chen Ji's lips curved: these people do have some discernment.

choices.description: Let them carry the news that 'Chen Ji is not dead' back, creating chaos in the Empire's plans.

text.content: Chen Ji didn't follow up; instead, he stepped back several paces, a meaningful smile playing at the corner of his mouth. The Empire's interior was never united—this news, once transmitted back, would surely cause the Crown Prince's Grand Tutor no end of trouble. His mood greatly improved, even wanting to hum a little tune—though this wasn't quite the appropriate setting.

dialogue.content: Just as everyone was in heated discussion, Ling Yuan suddenly raised his head, his gaze like lightning sweeping toward the edge of the crowd—precisely where Chen Ji was hiding. He walked over slowly, each step seemingly landing on everyone's heartbeat. 'This old man just sensed something unusual.' His voice wasn't loud, yet it clearly reached everyone's ears. 'Do you all know that Chen Ji's cultivation technique was uniquely different? His corpse would never be so... ordinary.'

text.content: The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor, as if receiving divine aid, immediately jumped out to agree: 'Exactly what Sect Master Ling said! This one felt something was off just now—this corpse was far too easy to deal with.' He wiped the cold sweat from his forehead, glaring viciously at Han Lie. 'Someone must be falsifying, trying to confuse us all!' Han Lie rolled his eyes, too lazy to argue with this jumping clown, only staring at Ling Yuan's back, a trace of wariness flickering in his gaze.

Ling Yuan had already walked to three zhang away from where Chen Ji was hiding. His footsteps stopped, a playful curve forming at the corner of his mouth. 'Chen Ji ah Chen Ji, did you think a mere illusion formation could deceive this old man?' His voice suddenly turned ice-cold. 'The aura of the Tianji Record—I am too familiar with it. It would never allow its master to die so miserably!' Before the words even finished, he猛地raised his hand, a fierce palm wind directly slashing toward where Chen Ji hid!

dialogue.content: Ling Yuan stood with hands behind his back, a confident smile spreading across his aged face. 'Come out, Chen Ji.' His voice seemed to come from the Nine Netherworlds, carrying bone-penetrating coldness. 'This old man has waited for this day for a very long time.' The surrounding crowd looked at each other in bewilderment. The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor opened his mouth to say something, but was nailed to the spot by one glare from Ling Yuan, unable to move.

text.content: Silence reigned over the ruins. Everyone held their breath, their gazes shuttling between Ling Yuan and that patch of shadow. Han Lie unconsciously clenched his fists tighter, and the disciples of the Xuanwu Sect all activated their spiritual energy in戒备. The air was filled with an oppressive sense of an impending storm, as if something earth-shattering was about to happen at any moment. Ling Yuan's palm wind had yet to dissipate, raising countless dust particles, lifting everyone's hearts to their throats.

dialogue.content: Ling Yuan looked around at the various faces—some frightened, some confused—before suddenly bursting into laughter. 'What, all scared?' He laughed so hard his body shook, even producing tears. 'A bunch of idiots! Being played for fools by atrash!' He pointed at the charred corpse. 'Did you really think Chen Ji died? He's been watching your show from beginning to end!' At these words, the entire crowd erupted. The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor's face turned ashen, Han Lie's brow furrowed tightly, and the scattered cultivators discussed in whispers, not daring to believe their ears.

text.content: Ling Yuan's laughter cut off abruptly. He looked around at the faces—some frightened, some confused—and a trace of mockery flickered in his eyes. 'Idiots.' He whispered. 'Such a bunch of idiots.' He turned to the Crown Prince's Grand Tutor, his gaze sharp as a blade. 'You say you killed Chen Ji? Then where is the Heavenly Fate residue on the corpse? When a Tianji Record inheritor dies, their body leaves a unique Heavenly Fate imprint—did you see it?' The Crown Prince's Grand Tutor's mouth opened but no words came out, cold sweat dripping down profusely. 'And you, Han Lie.' Ling Yuan looked at Han Lie. 'You've fought him several times—when did you ever truly gain the upper hand? Every time he was in 'dire peril,' yet in the end he always stood. Did you ever wonder why?' Han Lie's face was ashen, his fists clenched so tight they cracked. Ling Yuan threw his head back and laughed, his laughter echoing above the ruins. 'He's not dead—you're all idiots!'
